questions.prompt: Why should a 1 kHz motor loop run on a microcontroller rather than on Linux on a Raspberry Pi?
options: Linux scheduling is best effort, so an iteration can be late.
Linux cannot run Python fast enough to add two numbers in 1 ms.
A Raspberry Pi has no GPIO pins, so it cannot drive anything.
Microcontrollers always have more RAM than a single-board computer.
questions.explanation: A motor loop needs its deadline every time. A bare-metal MCU with timer interrupts gives it; Linux shares the CPU among many tasks.

questions.prompt: Step size of a 12-bit ADC with a 3.3 V reference, in millivolts. Precision 0.005.
20-byte frames at 200 Hz on a 115200 baud 8N1 UART. Link load as a fraction. Precision 0.002.
A 14-byte I2C register burst read (address, register, repeated start, address, 14 data bytes, 9 clocks per byte) on a 400 kHz bus. Time in microseconds. Precision 1.
Which bus uses a differential twisted pair, 120 ohm terminators at both ends and message IDs for priority?
questions.explanation: CAN arbitrates by message ID on a differential pair terminated at both ends.

questions.prompt: Worst-case length in bits of a classic 11-bit-ID CAN data frame with 8 data bytes, including bit stuffing and intermission.
A 5 V sensor output must go to an ESP32 input (3.3 V logic, not 5 V tolerant). What is a sound fix for a one-way signal?
options: Connect it directly: the ESP32 clamps the extra voltage safely.
Add a pull-up resistor to 3.3 V on the input.
Raise the ESP32 supply to 5 V so levels match.
Use a 1 kohm over 2 kohm divider, or a level shifter.
questions.explanation: A divider turns 5 V into about 3.33 V. Direct connection can damage the pin.

questions.prompt: A robot has a camera, a 2D LiDAR, two wheel motors and an IMU. Propose compute and buses and justify the split.
rubric: Puts ROS 2, camera and LiDAR on an SBC and the fast motor and IMU loop on an MCU, with a reason (best effort against hard real-time).
Chooses a bus for each link (UART or USB between SBC and MCU, I2C or SPI for the IMU, Ethernet or USB for the LiDAR) with wires and speed in mind.
Checks the load of the busiest link against about 50 % and says what would change the plan.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
